import pandas as pd
import os

# Read the input raw data
input_path = "outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv"
df = pd.read_csv(input_path)

# Identify indicator columns
# The raw data is in long format with columns: city_id, city_name, year, indicator_id, value
# We need to pivot it to wide format

# Get all unique indicator_ids
indicator_ids = df['indicator_id'].unique()

# Pivot the data
# city_id, city_name, year as index
# indicator_id as columns
# value as values
pivot_df = df.pivot_table(
    index=['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'],
    columns='indicator_id',
    values='value',
    aggfunc='first'  # Assuming one value per city/year/indicator
)

# Reset index to make city_id, city_name, year regular columns
pivot_df = pivot_df.reset_index()

# Sort by city_id and year for consistency
pivot_df = pivot_df.sort_values(by=['city_id', 'year']).reset_index(drop=True)

# Ensure all indicator columns are present and in a consistent order
# Reorder columns: city_id, city_name, year, then indicator columns sorted by indicator_id
indicator_cols = sorted([c for c in pivot_df.columns if c not in ['city_id', 'city_name', 'year']])
ordered_cols = ['city_id', 'city_name', 'year'] + indicator_cols
pivot_df = pivot_df[ordered_cols]

# Write to output
output_path = "outputs/t11_city_indicator_matrix.csv"
pivot_df.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

print(f"Output written to {output_path}")
print(f"Shape: {pivot_df.shape}")
print(f"Columns: {list(pivot_df.columns)}")
</solution_file>
